Host Jure notes in the introduction that this triumph offered a special pleasure because the match in many elements was reminiscent of authentic derbies from times past: a rainstorm, a sirocco turning into a bura, the north stand tucked under the downpour, smoke and interruptions.\n\nDanko and Mate emphasize the historical weight of the comeback at Poljud, drawing parallels with iconic victories from the past and emphasizing that the victory under the leadership of coach Garcia had exceptional psychological weight for entering the demanding autumn schedule. Mate emphasizes that with this victory, Garcia took the pressure of the public off regarding derby outcomes, directing the team's focus toward stability and self-confidence before the upcoming European tests.",

Dinamo's play was reduced to isolated attempts, and only the quality of the back line along with Beljo's attacking class prevented an earlier collapse of the visitors. Garcia, according to Mate's words, won the match through the preparation of the structure and the introduction of quality interline solutions, with Šotiček functioning as a player whom Dinamo's defense simply failed to catch or close down.",

The left side of the attack attracted all of Dinamo's attention, forcing Dominguez into constant patching up and stepping out, which consequently opened space for isolation on the opposite side of the pitch.\n\nBamba played a match on the right wing that put Dinamo's left side of defense through unbearable trouble.      "content": "Hajduk's quick return to the match prevented the psychological collapse that the team used to experience in previous seasons. The main architect of the equalizer was Šimun Hrgović.      "content": "After a bizarre situation at the end of the first half in which Šotiček nearly punished the uncertainty of Dinamo goalkeeper Kotarski, Hajduk entered the second half in a hurricane rhythm. In the first twenty minutes of the restart, the Split team won as many as 14 out of 17 duels, literally forcing Dinamo into panicked clearances and a complete disruption of any meaningful attack organization.\n\nThe crowning achievement of such dominance was the winning goal for 2:1, which Jure describes as a superbly rehearsed automatism of the team. Hrgović found Šego in the pocket of space, Šego timely avoided offside and, with his back turned to the goal, calmly laid the ball off for Bamba, who runs in from the second plan and hits the net. Mate underlines that Hajduk's high pressing – in which Šego, Šotiček, and Bamba synchronously closed passing angles for Dinamo's back line – extinguished every idea of Dinamo's build-up and confirmed the complete tactical victory of the Split team.",

In addition, he won as many as nine out of twelve duels.
